workflow_hypothesis: Pending lexical error is misinterpreted as normal end-of-input
pattern: Error-bearing end-of-input sentinels are mistaken for clean input exhaustion during tokenization.
description: A layered tokenizer fails to distinguish normal end-of-input from an end-of-input sentinel returned alongside a pending lexical error.
precondition: A tokenizer processes malformed input whose state transition, such as indentation handling, reaches an invalid embedded byte that the low-level reader can report through an end-of-input sentinel plus an error state.
critical_operation: The tokenizer interprets the reader result and decides whether to finish the current token or propagate a lexical error.
interference: The reader uses the same sentinel value for both clean exhaustion and invalid-byte detection while recording the latter as a pending error.
invalid_assumption: Any end-of-input sentinel is safe to treat as ordinary completion, without checking whether an error is pending.
failure: The tokenizer emits or constructs a normal token while the error remains pending, causing an internal invariant failure instead of a recoverable tokenization error.
search_strategy: Inspect every branch handling an end-of-input sentinel from a lower-level reader and check the pending error state before treating it as clean exhaustion.
Trace error propagation from character reading through token emission and verify that no token result is constructed while an error is pending.
Add malformed-input tests combining indentation or other state transitions with an embedded terminator or invalid byte, and assert a lexical error rather than an internal failure.
Audit token-result constructors for callers that may receive sentinel-derived output and require explicit error propagation instead of a global error-state workaround.

evidence.supports: A malformed indented input containing an embedded zero byte caused the character reader to return an end-of-input value with an error set; the tokenizer then allowed normal token construction to proceed, producing an internal system failure. scope_note: This cluster contains one report, so the pattern is cautiously scoped to layered tokenizers or similar incremental parsers where a low-level reader conflates clean exhaustion with error-bearing sentinel results.
